active.title: Ice Skate at Patinoire Poseidon
active.description: Woluwe's municipal rink runs public sessions year-round — cheap skate rental, questionable Eurodance on the speakers, and Brussels families wobbling alongside you like it's 1987.
active.bonus: One full lap skating backwards before you leave — falling counts as trying.

active.title: Swim Laps at the Néptunium, Schaerbeek
active.description: Schaerbeek's restored Art Deco municipal bath has been splashing Brusselaers for generations — no-nonsense lane swimming under a soaring vaulted hall that most of the city forgot exists.
active.bonus: Complete 20 consecutive lengths without stopping, then reward yourself with a coffee at the poolside bar.

active.title: Morning swim at the Forest National pool
active.description: The large public pool in Forest opens early and is mostly serious swimmers — go for a long-course 50m session and remember what good lane discipline feels like.

active.title: Friday Night Skate route through Brussels
active.description: Every Friday night from May onward, hundreds of skaters take over Brussels' streets in a police-led 20km loop — rent blades, join the mass, and feel the city differently.
active.bonus: Keep up with the front group. Don't fall behind.

active.title: Tennis in the Parc du Cinquantenaire
active.description: The triumphal arch park has bookable clay courts surrounded by green — a morning match in a European capital park is a very good way to start the day.
active.bonus: Play one set against a stranger you find at the park.

active.title: Cycle the Brussels–Bruges canal towpath
active.description: The flat canal towpath to Bruges is one of Europe's great cycling day trips — 100km of almost entirely traffic-free path through the Flemish countryside.
active.bonus: Make it to Bruges and eat frites before the train back.

active.title: Run the perimeter of Bois de la Cambre
active.description: The urban forest at the bottom of Avenue Louise has a flat perimeter loop beloved by Brussels runners — 5km through trees with a lake in the middle.
active.bonus: Run it twice. The second loop is always faster.

active.title: Bouldering at Arkose gym in Anderlecht
active.description: Brussels' best bouldering gym is in a converted industrial building in Anderlecht — rent shoes at the desk and start on the green routes.
active.bonus: Finish one route above your usual grade before you leave.

active.title: Walk all the way around Laeken royal park
active.description: The vast royal estate at Laeken has public perimeter trails through formal gardens, parkland, and the Atomium view — a full loop is about 8km.
active.bonus: Time the full loop and try to beat your time on the way back.

active.title: Five-a-Side Football at Aspria Arts–Loi
active.description: Show up to the open five-a-side sessions at Aspria near the European Quarter and you'll find a rotating cast of EU staffers, local students, and expats who all play harder than you expect.
active.bonus: Score a goal and celebrate it as if you've just won the World Cup — full performance, no apology.

active.title: Bike the Promenade Verte Circuit
active.description: The 60km Promenade Verte loops the entire Brussels Capital Region through forests, parks, and villages that feel nothing like the city center you left an hour ago.
active.bonus: Complete the full 60km loop without using any navigation app — paper map or nothing.

active.title: Early Morning Run Along the Canal to Laeken
active.description: Running Brussels' canal north from Sainte-Catherine to the Laeken greenhouses before the city wakes is the fastest way to understand the city's industrial-to-royal geography.
active.bonus: Stop at the Atomium on the return and do 10 burpees in front of it before anyone intervenes.

chill.title: The Three Weeks of the Serres Royales
chill.description: The royal greenhouses of Laeken — a glass city of domes and galleries dripping with century-old camellias — open to the public for only about three weeks each spring. Belgians plan around it.
chill.bonus: Go on a weekday morning at opening and walk the full circuit twice — once for the plants, once for the glass.

chill.title: Antique flea market at Place du Jeu de Balle
chill.description: The daily Marolles flea market is the real Brussels — comic books, silverware, vintage cameras, and decades of city life piled on folding tables.
chill.bonus: Find one thing under €5 that has a story you can invent.

chill.title: Magritte Museum morning
chill.description: The world's largest collection of Magritte works in a beautiful neoclassical building — go slow, read every caption, and pick one painting to sit in front of for ten minutes.
chill.bonus: Pick your favorite painting and be able to defend why.

chill.title: Art Nouveau architecture walk in Ixelles
chill.description: Brussels has more Art Nouveau buildings per square kilometer than any city on earth — Ixelles is where Victor Horta's students went wild on private houses.
chill.bonus: Photograph the details: ironwork, mosaic tiles, bay windows. Build a set.

chill.title: Slow morning coffee in a Saint-Boniface café
chill.description: Saint-Boniface square is Brussels at its most quietly livable — arrive before the lunch rush, order twice, and watch the neighbourhood come and go.
chill.bonus: Bring something to read. No scrolling.

chill.title: Afternoon in the Jardin du Roi with frites
chill.description: The Botanical Garden-adjacent park south of the city is Brussels' quietest green space — get a cone of frites from a nearby friterie and eat on the grass.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your bag for the whole visit.

chill.title: Comics hunt at Brüsel, Rue Fossé aux Loups
chill.description: Belgium invented the graphic novel as a serious medium — find a café that stocks them, order something Trappist, and read an entire Tintin or Blake & Mortimer volume.
chill.bonus: Pick one you've never read. Finish it in the café.

chill.title: Canal walk from Sainte-Catherine to Laeken
chill.description: The Brussels canal corridor has been quietly transformed into one of the best walks in the city — cafés, barges, and bridges the whole way.
chill.bonus: Count the barges moored along the way.

chill.title: Chocolate workshop at Planète Chocolat, Rue du Lombard
chill.description: Several Brussels chocolatiers run 90-minute workshops where you make your own pralines — you leave with a box of something genuinely excellent.
chill.bonus: Make an extra piece for someone specific.

chill.title: Comics Afternoon at Centre Belge de la Bande Dessinée
chill.description: The Belgian Comic Strip Center in a restored Horta building is one of the strangest, most specifically Belgian pleasures in a city full of them.
chill.bonus: Find a Tintin original panel on display and recreate the character's exact pose for a photo.

chill.title: Stroll and Sit in Parc du Cinquantenaire
chill.description: The Cinquantenaire's triumphal arch and manicured lawns are Brussels at its most imperial and unhurried — bring nothing and do absolutely nothing structured.
chill.bonus: Find a spot of grass with a direct sightline to the arch, lie flat on your back, and stay there for 20 minutes minimum.

chill.title: Read at Café Walvis, Molenbeek
chill.description: Walvis is a neighbourhood brown café in Molenbeek with mismatched chairs, Belgian draught, and exactly zero reasons to check your phone.
chill.bonus: Leave whatever book or magazine you brought on the table for the next person when you leave.

adventure.title: Day Trip to the Villers Abbey Ruins
adventure.description: Forty minutes by train, the roofless Gothic nave of Villers-la-Ville stands open to the sky — 800 years of Cistercian stone with vines growing through the windows and hardly anyone around on weekdays.
adventure.bonus: Find the abbey's own microbrewery beer in the shop and drink it inside the ruins.

adventure.title: Escape the Crowds at Musée des Instruments de Musique, Rooftop Bar
adventure.description: The MIM rooftop terrace above the Old England Art Nouveau building serves drinks with one of the highest and least-crowded panoramas over the Lower Town.
adventure.bonus: Pick up the headphone audio guide inside, find the weirdest instrument on display, and demonstrate its playing motion to whoever you're with.

adventure.title: Night Photography at Gare Centrale, Place de l'Albertine
adventure.description: Victor Horta's grand railway terminus glows like a sci-fi cathedral after midnight when commuters vanish and the Art Deco vaulting is all yours.
adventure.bonus: Shoot a long-exposure of an arriving train from the platform end without using a tripod.

adventure.title: Walk the Sewers at the Musée des Égouts
adventure.description: Brussels' Sewer Museum at Porte d'Anderlecht sends you down into the actual working 19th-century network under the Senne — Haussmann-scale infrastructure you walk through, smell included.
adventure.bonus: Go the entire tour without covering your nose — embrace it.

adventure.title: The Thousand Costumes at GardeRobe MannekenPis
adventure.description: A dedicated museum on Rue du Chêne holds over 1,000 costumes belonging to the world's most absurd civic mascot — Elvis, samurai armor, national dress from a hundred countries — stranger and more compelling than it has any right to be.
adventure.bonus: Pick the costume you would dress him in and make your case to a stranger in the room.

adventure.title: Street Art Maze in Molenbeek, Rue de Manchester
adventure.description: The canal-side blocks around Rue de Manchester hide one of Europe's densest concentrations of politically charged murals, with zero tourist foot traffic.
adventure.bonus: Find a mural with text in three different languages and read each one aloud on the spot.

adventure.title: Royal Crypt and Laeken Cemetery
adventure.description: Notre-Dame de Laeken guards the crypt of Belgium's kings, and the cemetery behind it — Brussels' Père-Lachaise — holds a cast of Rodin's Thinker brooding over the graves.
adventure.bonus: Find and photograph the oldest legible inscription on a burial slab — share it with no caption.

adventure.title: Ardennes forest day trip hike
adventure.description: The Belgian Ardennes is 90 minutes south — forested valleys, castle ruins, and river gorges that feel nothing like a capital city weekend.
adventure.bonus: Make it to at least one castle ruin before you turn back.

adventure.title: Urban Bouldering at Arkose Brussels
adventure.description: Arkose in Molenbeek is the city's sharpest climbing gym — high-quality routes, a strong local scene, and a post-climb natural wine bar that makes the whole thing feel very Brussels.
adventure.bonus: Ask a stranger on the wall to show you the hardest route they can currently complete and attempt it.

adventure.title: Forest de Soignes Night Walk
adventure.description: The beech cathedral of Soignes after dark turns one of Europe's most underrated urban forests into something genuinely cinematic and slightly unnerving.
adventure.bonus: Stand completely still for 60 seconds in total darkness away from any path and just listen.

adventure.title: Canal Kayak from Tour & Taxis
adventure.description: Paddling the Brussels canal from the repurposed Tour & Taxis freight depot gives you a water-level view of industrial heritage that no tour bus can touch.
adventure.bonus: Wave at someone eating on a canal-side terrace and get them to wave back.

adventure.title: Rooftop Sprint at the Atomium
adventure.description: Belgium's most surreal landmark earns its reputation up close — the panoramic top sphere at 92 meters reframes the entire city in steel and sky.
adventure.bonus: Find the oldest date stamped on any information panel inside and photograph it.

social.title: Sundown Pétanque at Parc Josaphat, Schaerbeek
social.description: Parc Josaphat's dedicated pétanque lanes fill with Schaerbeek locals every evening — join an ongoing game and you will drink, argue, and leave with friends.
social.bonus: Challenge the winning team immediately after their game ends — no introductions, just point at the court.

social.title: Night market at Tour & Taxis
social.description: The vast former railway depot hosts Brussels' biggest night market events — food trucks, live music, design stalls, and the kind of crowd that makes you glad you came.
social.bonus: Eat something from every continent available. Check the stalls first.

social.title: Evening drinks on Place Luxembourg, EU Quarter
social.description: Walk the EU institutions quarter, marvel at the density of bureaucracy in a single neighbourhood, and end at a café full of Eurocrats with their badges still on.
social.bonus: Ask someone in a blazer what they actually do.

social.title: Afternoon at KANAL-Centre Pompidou, Tour & Taxis
social.description: Molenbeek has transformed into one of Brussels' most interesting art districts — check listings for opening nights and walk in cold.
social.bonus: Talk to the artist if they're there. Ask what the piece is actually about.

social.title: Aperitivo hour at Place du Châtelain
social.description: Wednesday evenings the square fills with after-work Brussels — find a terrace table, order something Belgian, and let the evening happen without a plan.
social.bonus: Talk to the people at the next table.

social.title: Comic book mural hunt through the city center
social.description: Brussels has 50+ officially sanctioned comic strip murals hidden on building walls across the city — get the map from the tourist office and find as many as you can.
social.bonus: Find Tintin first, then see how many others you can name.

social.title: DJ night at Fuse Club, Ixelles
social.description: Brussels has a genuinely good underground club scene concentrated in Ixelles — find a basement with no line and go in without knowing the artist.
social.bonus: Stay for at least three songs before deciding if you like it.

social.title: Craft beer at Moeder Lambic Fontainas, Place Fontainas
social.description: Brussels has several bars with serious vintage pinball and arcade machine collections — challenge strangers to a game and work your way through the craft tap list.
social.bonus: Get the high score on at least one machine.

social.title: Aperitivo Hour at Le Comptoir des Galeries
social.description: The bar inside the Hotel des Galeries draws Brussels' creative and media crowd at golden hour — perfectly made Negronis, no tourists, sharp conversation.
social.bonus: Start a conversation with whoever is sitting alone at the bar and find out what they actually do for work.

social.title: Political Debate Night at Théâtre National
social.description: The Théâtre National regularly stages public forum nights and politically charged performances that remind you Brussels is an actual capital, not just a chocolate shop.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to one stranger during the interval and ask them the most provocative political question you can think of.

social.title: Karaoke at Le You Club
social.description: Le You is Brussels' most committed late-night karaoke bar — deep Ixelles, a crowd that treats every song like a finale, and enough Belgian beer to get you on stage.
social.bonus: Sing an entire song in French even if you don't speak a word of it.

social.title: Late Night at Delirium Café
social.description: Delirium holds a Guinness record for beer selection — 2,000+ labels — and its labyrinthine basement fills nightly with an international crowd that actually knows what they're ordering.
social.bonus: Let a stranger at the bar pick your next beer without telling them your budget.

foodie.title: Single-origin chocolate tasting at Pierre Marcolini
foodie.description: The Belgian chocolatier who sources cacao like a sommelier sources wine — sit at the tasting counter and work through origins from Peru to Madagascar.
foodie.bonus: Pick one for someone back home and actually bring it to them.

foodie.title: Belgian beer flight at a brown café in the Pentagone
foodie.description: Old Brussels cafés with dark wood, tiled floors, and a 200-beer menu are a category unto themselves — drink chronologically from blond to tripel to Gueuze.
foodie.bonus: Find a beer you've never seen anywhere else and order two.

foodie.title: Belgian waffle at Gaufres de Bruxelles, Grand Place
foodie.description: Liège waffles are chewy, caramelized, and built to be eaten standing — find one near the Matonge African quarter and eat it without toppings.
foodie.bonus: Eat it plain. The pearl sugar is the topping.

foodie.title: Tasting menu at Bon Bon, Uccle
foodie.description: The Sablon district holds some of the most quietly serious cooking in Europe — book weeks ahead and eat somewhere that requires your full attention.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair the wine without your input. Trust them.

foodie.title: Waterzooi at De Ultieme Hallucinatie, Rue Royale
foodie.description: The stew of the old Flemish cities — chicken or fish in a cream-vegetable broth — is Brussels comfort food at its most specific and uncompromising.
foodie.bonus: Ask the waiter which version they think is better: chicken or fish.

foodie.title: Jenever at À la Mort Subite, Bruxelles
foodie.description: The Dutch-Belgian grain spirit that predates gin by centuries comes young, old, and aged — a tasting flight is an hour of underrated pleasure.
foodie.bonus: Order the oldest expression on the menu and sip it slowly.

foodie.title: Sunday brunch at Châtelain market
foodie.description: The weekly market at Place du Châtelain fills with vendors, organic produce, and people eating on the square — show up late morning with no plan.
foodie.bonus: Only buy things from producers, not resellers.

foodie.title: Moules-frites at Aux Armes de Bruxelles, Grand Place
foodie.description: A pot of mussels in white wine, a cone of double-fried chips with mayo, and a glass of blonde — this is the brussels meal you do once and then always again.
foodie.bonus: Use an empty mussel shell as your fry scoop. It's the rule.

foodie.title: Trappist beer at In't Spinnekopke, Place du Jardin aux Fleurs
foodie.description: Belgium has six Trappist breweries; Brussels has restaurants that pair every course with the monks' output — find one and let beer replace wine for a night.
foodie.bonus: Identify which Trappist is your favorite before the bill arrives.

foodie.title: Dim Sum Crawl in Quartier Chinois
foodie.description: The blocks around Rue Sainte-Catherine hide a genuinely good Cantonese scene — dim sum carts, roast duck windows, and bubble tea joints that Brussels tourists almost never find.
foodie.bonus: Order one dish entirely by pointing at someone else's table without knowing what it is.

foodie.title: Sunday Market Brunch at Flagey
foodie.description: The Sunday organic market around Place Flagey in Ixelles pulls the best producers from across Belgium — graze on raw milk cheese, charcuterie, and sourdough while Ixelles slowly wakes up around you.
foodie.bonus: Spend exactly €15 and build the best possible picnic — no supermarket backup allowed.

foodie.title: Gueuze Tasting at Cantillon Brewery
foodie.description: Cantillon is a living lambic brewery in Anderlecht where you drink funky, spontaneously fermented gueuze straight from barrels in the actual production space.
foodie.bonus: Buy a bottle of Kriek and carry it openly through the Midi neighborhood on your way home.

foodie.title: Frites at Maison Antoine, Place Jourdan
foodie.description: Maison Antoine's double-fried frites with andalouse sauce from a paper cone on Place Jourdan is the single most honest meal Brussels will ever hand you.
foodie.bonus: Order three different sauces and rank them out loud to the person next to you in the queue.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Bozar Restaurant
foodie.description: Housed inside Horta's art nouveau masterpiece, Bozar serves technically precise Belgian cuisine that matches the architecture's quiet ambition course for course.
foodie.bonus: Ask the sommelier to pair a Belgian natural wine you've never heard of to your main and trust them completely.
